name: QuickBooks Online
tagline: Small-business accounting, invoicing, expenses, payroll add-ons, and tax workflows

pricing.notes: Official Intuit pricing checked 2026-07-30; Simple Start standard monthly price shown around $38/month, excluding time-limited promos.

verdictSummary: You can build invoicing and expense tables, but QuickBooks' value is accounting correctness, bank feeds, payroll/tax ecosystem, accountant workflows, compliance, and support.
coreLoopDIY: For simple needs, build invoice creation, payment tracking, expenses, CSV bank import, and basic P&L reports.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because accounting mistakes and tax messes cost more than the subscription.

priorArt.name: Akaunting
priorArt.desc: Open-source accounting software for invoicing, expenses, and small-business books.

alternatives.name: ERPNext
alternatives.desc: A real accounting ERP with invoices, expenses, reconciliation, inventory and payroll; setup is a small IT department in miniature.

alternatives.name: Manager Desktop
alternatives.desc: A complete desktop ledger with invoices, reconciliation, expenses and inventory; teamwork stops at the file.

alternatives.name: Bigcapital
alternatives.desc: Modern double-entry books, bills, expenses and inventory in Docker; bank feeds are still your problem to arrange.

alternatives.name: LedgerSMB
alternatives.desc: Serious double-entry accounting with quotes, stock, projects and reports; the interface does not audition for lifestyle ads.

alternatives.name: Frappe Books
alternatives.desc: Local books with invoices, bills, payments and a real ledger; collaboration ends where the SQLite file begins.

alternatives.name: Odoo Accounting — One App Free
alternatives.desc: A full hosted accounting app for zero dollars; install one unrelated Odoo app and the free ride ends.

alternatives.name: Dolibarr
alternatives.desc: Invoices, banking, stock and double-entry books in one practical suite; payroll is explicitly not invited.

alternatives.name: GnuCash
alternatives.desc: Industrial-strength double entry, invoicing and reports on a desktop; friendly is not one of the accounting standards.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Akaunting
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free base is single-entry unless you buy the Double-Entry app, and the repo is BSL rather than open source.

notes: Essential no/kinda: the UI is cloneable, financial trust is not.
prompt:
Build me a bookkeeping-lite app covering the safe personal slice of QuickBooks
Online: invoicing a few clients and tracking expenses. Requirements:

- A local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3, binds to localhost, no
  hosting.
- Invoices: client, line items, tax rate, due date; render to PDF with
  Playwright's page.pdf; a manual mark-paid flag.
- Expenses: import my bank's CSV export, categorize with a rules table that
  auto-matches repeat payees, edit the rest by hand.
- Reports: a cash-basis P&L and per-quarter totals, plus CSV export of
  everything for the accountant.
- No accounts, no telemetry, the books never leave my machine; write a nightly
  dated backup copy of the SQLite file.
- Out of scope: bank feeds, reconciliation, payroll, and anything that files
  taxes. Do not build tax logic of any kind.
- README: state plainly that this is bookkeeping-lite, not accounting.
  QuickBooks' real product is accounting correctness, bank feeds, and the
  accountant ecosystem, none of which this rebuilds; when the numbers start to
  matter, the honest move is real software or an accountant.
